question_stem:
Electrons in a beam are travelling at high speed in a vacuum. The electrons are incident on a metal target, causing X-ray radiation to be emitted.

The variation with wavelength $\lambda$ of the intensity $I$ of the emitted X-ray radiation is shown in Fig. 7.1.

{{figure:9702_w20_42_q07_figure_7_1}}

Fig. 7.1

Explain why:

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: there is a continuous distribution of wavelengths

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: at certain wavelengths, there are narrow peaks of increased intensity.
